validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, independently confirmed. P7785 is MountainWest Overthrust Pipeline, LLC's 'Westbound Compression Expansion Project', FERC Docket CP24-13-000, an NGA section 7(c) application filed 2023-11-02, certificated 2024-10-17 (189 FERC P 61,046 (2024)), placed into service 2025-11-13, adding 325,000 Dth/d (325 MMcf/d) of westbound firm transport via two new 15,900 HP turbine compressors at the existing Point of Rocks and Rock Springs stations (Sweetwater County, WY) plus a small (~1,400 ft / 0.27 mi) new-pipe interconnect component in Lincoln/Sweetwater Counties, WY. Corroborated by FOUR independent-publisher sources: FERC's own two Federal Register notices (2023 application, 2026 motion-to-vacate-in-part, which quotes the Certificate Order directly), EIA's federal dataset (two releases, one origin), and Williams' own FY2025 10-K. CLASSIFICATION: correctly gas transmission (Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission) -- an NGA section 7(c) interstate-pipeline-company certificate, not gathering/distribution/storage. See the PipelineType fill for a specific caveat about EIA's separate, differently-scoped 'Pipeline Type: Intrastate' field (crosses-state-border flag, not a functional classification) so a future researcher doesn't mistake that for a conflict. DUPLICATE / CLUSTER CHECK (the Equitrans precedent): P7785 is NOT a duplicate of sibling rows P6898 (MountainWest 'Main Line', 1,868 mi / 2,600 MMcf/d, a different system entirely -- Colorado-Wyoming-Utah mainline) or P6899 (MountainWest 'Overthrust', 261 mi / 2,800 MMcf/d, the parent SYSTEM this Project expands). P7785's own capacity (325 MMcf/d, a discrete FERC-authorized INCREMENT) is never conflated here with P6899's system-wide total (2,800 MMcf/d) -- each row's figure is independently sourced to its own scope (project vs. system), avoiding the portfolio-total-copied-onto-siblings failure mode. P6899's own shard independently reached the same in-service finding (its cross_row_leads[] entry flagged P7785 as likely now operating, sourced to the same Williams FY2025 10-K sentence used here) -- consistent, non-conflicting, concurrent research. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1='Williams Companies' 100% and Operator='MountainWest Overthrust Pipeline' both confirmed current (acquisition closed 2023-02-14, not disputed for this row). SPEC CAVEAT (not escalated to a contested concern): a genuine discrepancy exists between EIA's notes ('from Wamsutter to the Opal hub') and FERC's own Certificate Order language (a new delivery point 'near Overthrust's existing Roberson Compressor Station', interconnecting with Kern River Gas Transmission) for this Project's specific new delivery point -- resolved in the Location fill by preferring FERC's own order text as more authoritative and more specific to this Project (vs. EIA's likely-broader-system phrasing); noted here so a future auditor doesn't re-litigate it as an unflagged conflict. Similarly, EIA states 0.27 mi of new pipe vs. the sheet's LengthKnown=0.00 -- kept at 0.00 given the project's overwhelmingly compression-only scope, per the standing 'no new physical pipe -> LengthKnown=0' convention (see the Length fill). FORWARD-LOOKING CAVEAT: a motion to vacate part of the certificate (filed 2026-03-11, noticed 2026-04-13) is pending, covering ONLY an unbuilt, auxiliary pig-launcher at the existing 'Cabin 31' interconnect (delayed by a BLM right-of-way and a landowner negotiation) -- Overthrust states this facility is not needed for full Project capacity. This does not affect Status, Capacity, or StartYear1 staged here, but is worth a future researcher's attention if FERC rules on the motion (could produce a minor certificate-scope change, not a capacity or in-service change).
